name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Clay Fuller running for reelection
Harris outraised Fuller heavily but spent nearly all of it with little outside help
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The district's R+19 lean and Fuller's incumbency make this safely Republican despite Shawn Harris's large fundraising edge, which came with minimal outside support and left him with almost no cash on hand. Markets price a Republican win around 94%, consistent with a double-digit expected margin.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving Fuller could narrow the margin, though a Harris win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Georgia's 14th district is deeply Republican territory, and incumbent Clay Fuller is seeking reelection with the advantages that come with holding the seat. Fuller has raised about $1.8 million and drawn substantial outside support, though his cash-on-hand is modest at roughly $70,000. Prediction markets give him about a 94% chance of winning.

Democratic challenger Shawn Harris has raised far more money personally, over $8 million, but has almost nothing left on hand and faces significant outside opposition spending with little outside help of his own. The district's strong partisan lean and incumbency outweigh Harris's fundraising advantage, making this a safe Republican seat with an expected double-digit margin.
